Definition: from G1519 and G4198; to enter (literally or figuratively):--come (enter) in, go into.
BiblicalUsage: To go in is to enter a place or a heart, and the Gospels use it for both. Jesus enters the synagogue at Capernaum and teaches, the cares of the world enter in and choke the word, and no one lights a candle and puts it in a secret place, but on a candlestick, so that those who come in may see the light. Acts shows the lame man carried daily to the temple gate, asking alms of those entering in.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what enters my heart decides what grows there, because the cares of the world choke the word just as surely as a stone chokes a seed. I want the light to come in, and the cares to stay out.
